# Printing kubara

_Generated by `npm run print:report` on 2026-10-22 from the files in this folder. Numbers are measured, not guessed: geometry is analysed with manifold-3d, and if Bambu Studio is installed it slices the files with its command-line interface._

## At a glance

|  |  |
|---|---|
| Height | 80 mm figure + 2.93 mm base = **82.93 mm** |
| Footprint (base plate) | 53.24 x 54.89 mm |
| Solid volume | 99.49 cm³ (123.37 g if printed 100 % solid in PLA at 1.24 g/cm³) |
| Filament, normal settings | **≈ 41.65 g** PLA single colour, 3.09 g of it support (Bambu Studio slice, 1.28 h on an X1C) |
| Supports | **needed** under the chin and between the legs (3.09 g of tree supports); details below |
| Orientation | upright, standing on its base, as the files are already placed |
| Smallest safe size | 60 mm figure height with a 0.4 mm nozzle (set by the 1.17 mm mouth line; the structure itself holds down to 41 mm) |

## Files

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `kubara.stl` | single colour, one watertight shell, 80 mm figure on a 2.9 mm heptagon base |
| `kubara_120mm.stl` | the same body scaled ×1.5 (120 mm figure, 124.4 mm total) |
| `kubara_nobase.stl` | the bare figure, exactly 80 mm, flat soles (glue it on your own base or print with a brim) |
| `kubara_multicolor.3mf` | one object with 4 named parts, each pre-assigned to a filament slot (Bambu Studio / OrcaSlicer) |
| `parts/*.stl` | the 4 colour parts as separate STLs in one shared coordinate frame. Load them together to reassemble |
| `print-analysis.json` | every number in this document, machine-readable |

## Recommended slicer settings

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Orientation | Upright on the base. Do not rotate it: the base is the only flat face, and the upright pose keeps the supports off the face and the glasses. |
| Layer height | 0.16 mm or 0.20 mm (0.12 mm for a showpiece; the head is mostly gentle curves, so variable/adaptive layer height works well) |
| Nozzle | 0.4 mm. A 0.2 mm nozzle sharpens the mouth/nostrils at small scales |
| Walls | 3 walls (≈1.2 mm). The ears, paws and arms are then solid perimeters |
| Top / bottom | 5 top, 3-4 bottom layers |
| Infill | 10-15 % gyroid or grid. It is a figurine, so 15 % is plenty |
| Supports | Tree (auto) / organic, threshold 45°, top Z distance 0.2 mm, support interface 2 layers. See the next section |
| Brim | not needed (the base is 53.24 mm wide); use one only for kubara_nobase.stl |
| Material | PLA / PLA+ (all numbers assume PLA 1.24 g/cm³). PETG works but strings more on the face details |

## Supports: where and why

Overhangs were analysed programmatically on `kubara.stl` as placed (upright). Two methods were used:

1. **Facet analysis.** Every downward-facing triangle steeper than 45° from vertical (not touching the bed), grouped into connected patches and labelled by body region. Total: **955 mm²** of projected overhang area. Below 766 mm² of it there is only build plate or the figure's own base plate, so supports leave no visible marks there. Under the other 189 mm² a support column would have to stand on the figure itself (on the belly or a paw).
2. **Layer analysis**, done the way a slicer does it. The body is sliced every 0.2 mm, and the report records (a) islands that start in mid-air with nothing below them and (b) the area of each layer that sticks out more than a 45° slope beyond the layer below.

**Overhang zones (facet analysis):**

| Region | Height (mm) | Projected area (mm²) | Support would rest on |
|---|---|---|---|
| underside between the legs (crotch / rump) | 7.3–14.4 | 575 | build plate / base plate |
| chin / underside of the snout | 52.9–56.9 | 233 | the figure below (leaves marks) |
| toes (left foot) | 3.0–4.6 | 32 | build plate / base plate |
| toes (right foot) | 3.0–4.7 | 32 | build plate / base plate |
| under the right paw | 26.5–31.1 | 18 | build plate / base plate |
| under the left paw | 26.5–31.1 | 18 | build plate / base plate |
| back of the head / strap | 68.7–73.9 | 9 | the figure below (leaves marks) |

No floating islands: every layer touches the layer below.

**Largest unsupported zones (layer analysis):**

| Region | Height (mm) | Area beyond 45° (mm², summed over layers) |
|---|---|---|
| underside between the legs (crotch / rump) | 7.7–14.3 | 285 |
| chin / underside of the snout | 53.1–56.7 | 127 |
| toes (right foot) | 3.3–4.5 | 9 |
| toes (left foot) | 3.3–4.5 | 9 |
| between the feet / crotch | 7.7–8.1 | 3 |
| under the left paw | 26.7–27.9 | 3 |
| under the right paw | 26.7–27.9 | 3 |

**What Bambu Studio actually generated.** Tree supports at 45°, 3.09 g in total:

| Supports the | Height (mm) | Grams |
|---|---|---|
| chin / underside of the snout | 0.2–56.2 | 1.83 |
| underside between the legs (crotch / rump) | 3.4–14.2 | 1.26 |

**In practice:**

- Use **tree / organic supports**. A straight column under the chin would land on the belly, but tree supports branch around it: in the Bambu Studio slice the chin tree grows from the build plate (it starts at z = 0.2 mm), so "on build plate only" can stay on and the belly stays clean. The crotch supports stand on the base plate, which is hidden in use.
- The critical spot is **under the chin / snout**. It is the only large flat-ish ceiling, and the face is the most visible surface, so use 2 support interface layers and 0.2 mm top Z distance.
- Alternatively, set supports to "manual" and **paint** them only on the zones listed above (Bambu: Support painting, enforcer). Everything else, including the lenses, strap, arms and ears, is designed to print without support (45° chamfers under the lenses and strap, a hidden gusset under the paws).

**Orientation check.** Projected overhang area for other orientations (facet metric):

| Orientation | Overhang (mm²) | Flat bed contact (mm²) |
|---|---|---|
| upright on its base (as delivered) | 955 | 2080 |
| tilted back 20 deg | 3063 | 0 |
| lying on its back | 1875 | 3 |
| lying on its face | 2070 | 63 |
| upside down (on the ears) | 2967 | 1 |
| on its side | 2119 | 3 |

Upright is the only orientation with a real flat face on the bed (the 2080 mm² base). The other orientations rest on a curved surface, so they need a raft or a large support pad, and they leave support scars on visible areas.

|---|---|
| Figure / total height | 80 / 82.93 mm |
| Bounding box (x × y × z) | 53.24 × 54.89 × 82.93 mm |
| Surface area | 168.6 cm² |
| Solid volume | 99.49 cm³ → 123.37 g at 100 % (upper bound) |
| Geometric estimate, 3 walls + 15 % infill | ≈ 40.89 g + ≈ 2.02 g support |
| Bambu Studio slice, single colour, 80 mm | **41.65 g** (model 38.56 g + support 3.09 g), 1.28 h, 415 layers |
| Bambu Studio slice, single colour, 120 mm | **116.35 g** (support 8.98 g), 2.98 h |

Slicer numbers: Bambu Lab X1 Carbon 0.4 nozzle, "0.20mm Standard @BBL X1C", Bambu PLA Basic @BBL X1C with density overridden to 1.24 g/cm³, 3 walls, 15 % infill, tree(auto) supports at 45°. A P1S gives about the same time; an A1 / A1 mini is roughly 10-20 % slower.

## Multi-colour (AMS)

Open `kubara_multicolor.3mf` in Bambu Studio or OrcaSlicer. It loads as **one object with 4 parts** that are already assigned to filament slots 1-4. If the slicer asks, choose to import the geometry/settings. Check the slots and their colours:

| Slot | Part | Colour | What | Solid weight |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | fur | `#9BE0DF` | body fur, light mint / aqua | 109.83 g solid |
| 2 | fur_shade | `#21B3B4` | muzzle + inner ears, turquoise | 4.60 g solid |
| 3 | ink | `#0A0F0F` | sunglasses, strap, nostrils, mouth, base plate | 8.88 g solid |
| 4 | glint | `#FCFDFD` | lens glints (2 small dots) | 0.03 g solid |

Steps:
1. Load the 3MF. In the Objects list, expand "kubara" to see the parts fur / fur_shade / ink / glint and their filament numbers.
2. In the filament panel, set slot colours to match (e.g. Bambu PLA Basic *Mint* or *Ice Blue* for fur, *Turquoise* / *Cyan* for fur_shade, *Black*, *Jade White*). If the slicer shows only one filament, add filaments 2-4 with the **+** button. The part assignments stay.
3. Enable supports as above. Then, under the object's filament / flushing options, enable **"Flush into objects' infill"** and **"Flush into support"** to save purge filament. The prime tower is required for AMS.
4. Slice and check the preview in "Filament" colour mode.

Bambu Studio slice of the 3MF (80 mm, X1C, flush into infill + support enabled): **9.03 h**, **250 filament changes**, Bambu Studio reports **145.9 g** in total. Grams per slot, from the G-code (start-up purge included, so slightly more):

| Slot | Colour | Model | Support | Purge + prime tower | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | #9BE0DF | 28.8 | 3.1 | 51.1 | 82.9 |
| 2 | #21B3B4 | 3.9 | 0.1 | 44.0 | 48.0 |
| 3 | #0A0F0F | 6.8 | 0.1 | 13.5 | 20.4 |
| 4 | #FCFDFD | 0.3 | 0.0 | 6.3 | 6.6 |

So **39.83 g ends up in the figure** and **≈ 114.89 g is purge waste** (flush + prime tower). The colour changes cluster in the head, where every layer from the chin to the ears needs 2-4 colours.

Comparison (all 80 mm, X1C, same settings):

| Variant | Time | Filament changes | Filament (Bambu) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Single colour, `kubara.stl` | 1.3 h | 0 | 42 g |
| 4 colours, `kubara_multicolor.3mf` | 9.0 h | 250 | 146 g |
| 3 colours (glint part set to the ink slot, glints painted) | 8.1 h | 219 | 134 g |

Ways to cut the waste and time:

- Print the **glint** (slot 4) in the same white you would use anyway, or merge it into ink (set the glint part to slot 3) and add the glints with a white paint pen afterwards. That removes one colour from the busiest layers.
- Increase "flush into infill/support", or lower the flushing volumes (Bambu: Flushing volumes, multiplier 0.7-0.8 is usually fine going from dark to light only).
- Print a single-colour body and paint it (below). For one figurine this is often faster.
- No AMS: use the parts STLs with filament swaps at layer height (M600 / "Add pause"). Only the base (z 0–2.93 mm, ink) separates cleanly by height. The face colours are spread over the head, so true multi-colour needs an AMS / MMU / toolchanger.

## Paint it by hand (single-colour print)

Print `kubara.stl` in light mint/aqua PLA (or white/grey and paint everything). The design has painting guides moulded in:

- **Ink (black)**: the sunglasses, strap, nostrils and mouth all stand slightly proud of the surface, so a fine brush or a 0.7 mm black paint pen follows their edges easily. Paint the base black too.
- **Muzzle / inner ears (turquoise)**: the inner ears are recessed pockets. The muzzle has no moulded edge: paint the front block of the snout below the glasses (see `renders/print_mc_front.png`). Turquoise acrylic (e.g. a mix of phthalo turquoise + white) matches `#21B3B4`.
- **Glints**: one white dot on the upper outer corner of each lens (a white paint pen or a toothpick).
- Prep: remove support nubs under the chin with a flush cutter, sand with 400 grit, prime (spray filler primer hides layer lines), then acrylics. Finish with a matte varnish so the fur looks soft and the glasses with a gloss varnish.
- Palette: fur `#9BE0DF`, muzzle `#21B3B4`, ink `#0A0F0F`, glint `#FCFDFD`.

## Scaling

A ray-cast thickness probe (29595 samples, median of 5 rays each) measured the local wall thickness of `kubara.stl`. Only 0.30 % of the surface sits on less than 1.2 mm of material, and those spots are *feathered edges*: places where the strap, paws and soles blend into the body at a shallow angle and taper to zero along an attached edge. They are not protrusions and cannot break off. Per region, ignoring feathered edges (< 0.4 mm):

| Region | 1st percentile (mm) | 5th percentile (mm) | Median (mm) | Feathered |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ear | 1.22 | 2.35 | > 20 | 0.75 % |
| toes (foot) | 5.77 | 9.42 | 16.73 | 0.00 % |
| under the paw | 6.75 | 8.80 | > 20 | 0.21 % |
| arm / elbow | 8.49 | > 20 | > 20 | 0.00 % |
| back of the head / strap | 12.90 | > 20 | > 20 | 0.00 % |
| heel / sole (foot) | 14.09 | 14.39 | > 20 | 0.00 % |
| between the feet / crotch | 14.85 | 15.43 | > 20 | 0.00 % |
| inner thigh / hip | 16.31 | > 20 | > 20 | 0.00 % |

The thinnest real structures are the **ears**: 95 % of their surface sits on ≥ 2.35 mm of material at 80 mm (only the rounded rim is thinner). Everything else is chunky.

Designed detail widths at 80 mm (they scale linearly):

| Detail | Width (mm) |
|---|---|
| mouth / smile line (ink) | 1.17 |
| nostrils (ink) | 1.50 |
| finger / toe grooves (relief) | 1.50 |
| chin crease groove (relief) | 1.50 |
| lens glints (white) | 2.34 |
| glasses strap (ink) | 2.51 |

Scaling advice (figure height; the base scales with it):

- **Recommended minimum: 60 mm figure height** (×0.75) with a 0.4 mm nozzle.
- Structure: the ears stay ≥ 1.2 mm thick down to **41 mm**, and ≥ 0.8 mm (2 extrusion lines) down to **28 mm**. Below that they get fragile.
- **55 mm** is the smallest size where the finest colour/relief detail (1.17 mm wide at 80 mm) is still 2 lines wide with a 0.4 mm nozzle. With a 0.2 mm nozzle you can go to about **28 mm**.
- Scale **up** freely. At 120 mm (`kubara_120mm.stl`) use 0.2 mm layers and 3-4 walls. At 150 mm or more, 4 walls and 10 % infill keep the weight down.
- Always scale **uniformly** (lock the aspect ratio). In the multi-colour 3MF, scale the whole object, not individual parts.

`npm run render:print` writes these to `renders/` (project root):

- `print_mc_front.png`, `print_mc_three_quarter.png`, `print_mc_back.png`, `print_mc_face.png`: the 4 colour parts together, i.e. the AMS result

## Verification

Every mesh was re-read the way a slicer reads it (vertices welded by position) and checked for open edges, non-manifold edges, flipped faces and degenerate triangles, then reloaded into manifold-3d:

| File | Watertight | Shells | Triangles | Volume (cm³) | Size (mm) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| kubara.stl | yes | 1 | 116668 | 99.49 | 53.24 × 54.89 × 82.93 |
| kubara_nobase.stl | yes | 1 | 110986 | 93.42 | 48.65 × 52.25 × 80 |
| kubara_120mm.stl | yes | 1 | 107892 | 335.77 | 79.86 × 82.33 × 124.39 |
| parts/fur.stl | yes | 1 | 128474 | 88.58 | 48.65 × 44.79 × 80 |
| parts/fur_shade.stl | yes | 3 | 39642 | 3.71 | 31.7 × 41.31 × 26.79 |
| parts/glint.stl | yes | 2 | 3544 | 0.02 | 29.96 × 4.56 × 6.26 |
| parts/ink.stl | yes | 5 | 78966 | 7.16 | 53.24 × 54.89 × 79 |

- Colour parts: pairwise overlap 0.0083 mm³, outside the single body 0.0006 mm³. Together they make up the single body (99.47 vs 99.49 cm³; the parts are separated by a 0.01 mm gap so they never share faces).
- 3MF: **structurally valid**. Checked: content types, relationships, XML nesting, millimetre units, object ids, component and build references, colour group indices, model_settings ↔ components, project filament count, every part a closed 2-manifold identical to its parts/*.stl, parts disjoint (0.0083 mm³ overlap).
- Bambu Studio CLI round trip (import, then export project): all 4 parts kept their names and filament slots.

Regenerate everything with `npm run build && npm run print:report` (add `--no-slice` to skip Bambu Studio). Preview renders: `npm run render:print` → `renders/print_*.png`.
